title: Unify builder switchboard and prune stale build artifacts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our monorepo has accumulated several ad-hoc builder images, per-repo toolchain installs, and an explosion of cached build artifacts across CI agents. This increases image size, slows cold CI runs, and increases egress/storage cost for build caches. Goal: introduce a lightweight "builder switchboard" service and repository-level policy that centralizes toolchain selection, enables deterministic cache keys, and prunes stale artifacts automatically. The effort combines three themes: 1) standardize builder images and a shim that selects runtime/tool versions on-demand, 2) introduce TTL and tag-based pruning for remote cache (S3/CAS) and ephemeral runner caches, and 3) implement an artifact-pruning CI job plus a risk-controlled rollout to avoid build flakiness. This ticket coordinates implementation, infra changes, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: A1: All CI pipelines use the unified builder-switchboard image or shim; no repo-specific ad-hoc full tool installs remain
A2: Remote build cache (S3-backed CAS) supports TTL-based pruning and can delete artifacts older than policy without breaking builds
A3: Average cold CI job runtime for core services reduced by >= 25% on first-run (measured across 50 builds)
A4: Storage used by CI build artifacts reduced by >= 30% after 30 days of pruning (measured by bucket metrics)
A5: Rollout includes a canary group (10% of repos) with automatic rollback on regression detected by failing smoke tests
tasks: Design builder switchboard API and shim (selects node/python/rust/jdk version based on repo manifest)
Build minimal, layer-optimized builder images (base + language packs as small wheels) and publish to registry
Implement cache-key scheme for deterministic artifact keys (repo, commit, toolchain-version, input-hash)
Add server-side TTL and tag-based pruning to remote CAS (S3 lifecycle + index pruning job)
Add runner-side eviction policy for ephemeral local caches (LRU with size caps)
Create CI job 'ci/cleanup-artifacts' that runs weekly and prunes unreferenced artifacts older than TTL
Add monitoring dashboards: cache hit-rate, cold-start latency, storage bytes, pruning deletions
Run canary rollout for 10% of repos, collect regressions, and validate rollback mechanism
Document migration guide and provide per-repo quickfix scripts for repos that still require custom toolchains
comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Chen: Spike completed. PoC switchboard binary that reads .tool-versions and maps to pinned image tags. Observed initial cold-start improvement on node projects (~18%).

2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Design review notes: prefer content-addressed cache keys to avoid accidental collisions; add 'toolchain-version' to key. Also we should avoid deleting artifacts referenced by active PRs — use a reference-counting or lease approach.

2026-03-06 - Maya Chen: Infra note from SRE: S3 lifecycle alone is insufficient for immediate reclamation; we'll maintain an index (DynamoDB) for quick pruning and to track last-referenced timestamps. This adds small infra cost but enables safe delete orchestration.
2026-03-08 - Design feedback (Nadia Patel): Provide a fallback 'full-toolchain' builder image for legacy repos that can't migrate within the canary window. Limit usage and monitor.

2026-03-10 - QA (Diego Ramos): Proposed smoke test matrix added: build, run unit tests, run integration smoke that touches database migrations. Must be run on canary before enabling pruning for that repo.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented runner eviction and TTL policy in branch 'ci/switchboard-cache'. Performance tests scheduled against mainline tomorrow. Will open PR and link below.
